Violin plot of GBIF altitudes with the altitude of the samples

Source: R/plot_tax_alt_pq.R
plot_tax_alt_pq.Rd

<a href="https://adrientaudiere.github.io/MiscMetabar/articles/Rules.html#lifecycle"> <img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange" alt="lifecycle-experimental"></a>

For each taxon, draw the distribution of the altitudes of its GBIF occurrences as a violin, and the altitude of each sample in which the taxon is present as a horizontal line. The standardized effect size (SES) computed by [tax_alt_ses_pq()] is written above each violin, and taxa are ordered by SES.

Usage

plot_tax_alt_pq(
  physeq,
  sample_alt_col,
  occ_alt,
  taxonomic_rank = "currentCanonicalSimple",
  taxa_col = "canonicalName",
  elevation_col = "elevation",
  min_records = 10,
  order_by_ses = TRUE,
  show_ses = TRUE,
  sample_color = "#C0392B"
)

Arguments

physeq

(phyloseq, required) A phyloseq object with a `sam_data` slot.

sample_alt_col

(character, required) Name of the numeric column of the `sam_data` slot giving the altitude of each sample (in meters).

occ_alt

(data.frame, required) GBIF altitudes of the taxa, with one row per occurrence (as returned by [tax_gbif_alt()] with `return_raw = TRUE`), with columns `taxa_col` and `elevation_col`.

taxonomic_rank

(character, default `"currentCanonicalSimple"`) The column(s) of the `tax_table` giving the taxonomic names, matched against the `taxa_col` column of `occ_alt`. Can be a vector of two columns (e.g. `c("Genus", "Species")`).

taxa_col

(character, default `"canonicalName"`) Name of the column of `occ_alt` with the taxonomic names.

elevation_col

(character, default `"elevation"`) Name of the column of `occ_alt` with the occurrence altitudes (long format only).

min_records

(integer, default `10`) Minimum number of GBIF altitudes for a taxon to be plotted.

order_by_ses

(logical, default `TRUE`) If TRUE, taxa are ordered by increasing SES, else alphabetically.

show_ses

(logical, default `TRUE`) If TRUE, the SES is written above each violin.

sample_color

(character, default `"#C0392B"`) Color of the lines depicting the altitude of the samples.

Value

A ggplot2 object.

See also

[tax_alt_ses_pq()], [tax_gbif_alt()]

Author

Adrien Taudiere

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data_fungi_mini_cleanNames <- gna_verifier_pq(data_fungi_mini,
  data_sources = 11
)
# Requires GBIF credentials (see ?tax_gbif_alt)
occ_alt <- tax_gbif_alt(data_fungi_mini_cleanNames, return_raw = TRUE)

# data_fungi_mini has no altitude: add a fictive one
sample_data(data_fungi_mini_cleanNames)$altitude <-
  runif(nsamples(data_fungi_mini_cleanNames), 0, 1500)
plot_tax_alt_pq(data_fungi_mini_cleanNames, "altitude", occ_alt)
} # }
